### Setup project and run tests

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/packages/bun-plugin-yaml/README.md

Install dependencies and execute the test suite when contributing to the plugin.

```bash
$ bun install # project setup
$ bun test # run tests
```

--------------------------------

### Valid shortened import paths example setup

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/import/no-useless-path-segments.mdx

Demonstrates valid, simplified relative import paths in src/pages/home.js that are not reported.

```js
export function formatDate() {}
```

```js
export function Header() {}
```

```js
import { formatDate } from "../format.js";
import { Header } from "./header.js";
```

--------------------------------

### Setup logic in package.json bun-create section

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/templating/create.mdx

Specify pre- and post-install setup scripts in the "bun-create" section of a local template's package.json. preinstall and postinstall accept a string or an array of strings; arrays run in order. Commands run through the shell in the destination folder, and bun create stops with a non-zero code if a command or bun install fails.

```json
{
  "name": "@bun-examples/simplereact",
  "version": "0.0.1",
  "main": "index.js",
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^17.0.2",
    "react-dom": "^17.0.2"
  },
  "bun-create": {
    "preinstall": "echo 'Installing...'", // a single command
    "postinstall": ["echo 'Done!'"], // an array of commands
    "start": "bun run echo 'Hello world!'"
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Import and use node:http createServer and fetch

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/trimmed-is-whole/cases/built-in-modules.js.txt

Starts an HTTP server on a random port, fetches it, then closes the server.

```javascript
import http from "node:http";
const server = http.createServer((request, response) => response.end("ok"));
await new Promise(resolve => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
console.log(await (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}/`)).text());
server.close();
```

### Example output when using .prettierrc with plugins

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/format/migrate-from-prettier.mdx

Shows how Bun reports which files are formatted natively and which are passed to your installed Prettier when a .prettierrc config includes plugins.

```txt
Using .prettierrc (Prettier config)

    3 files are formatted natively
    1 file goes to your installed Prettier: 1 *.astro

Built-in plugins: @ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports
Plugins that use your installed Prettier: prettier-plugin-astro

Still needed:   @ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports, prettier, prettier-plugin-astro (some files go to them)
```

--------------------------------

### Valid single and nested hooks example

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/bun-test/no-duplicate-hooks.mdx

Demonstrates valid hook usage by combining setup actions into a single `beforeEach` per block or isolating them into nested `describe` blocks.

```ts
import { beforeEach, describe, test } from "bun:test";

describe("cart", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cart.clear();
    cart.add("apple");
  });

  test("has one item", () => {});

  describe("after checkout", () => {
    beforeEach(() => {
      cart.checkout();
    });

    test("is empty", () => {});
  });
});

```

--------------------------------

### Install Bun in GitHub Actions with setup-bun

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/install/cicd.mdx

Use the official oven-sh/setup-bun action in a GitHub Actions runner step to install Bun and execute commands like bun install.

```yaml
name: my-workflow
jobs:
  my-job:
    name: my-job
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # ...
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 # [!code ++]

      # run any `bun` or `bunx` command
      - run: bun install # [!code ++]
```

### Example server.ts for trim analysis

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/compiler/size.mdx

Sample program used to demonstrate `--explain=trim` output. It starts a Bun.serve server on port 3000 and logs a listening message.

```ts
Bun.serve({
  port: 3000,
  routes: { "/": () => new Response("hello") },
});
console.log("listening");
```

### Valid label references without whitespace

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/markdown/no-invalid-label-refs.mdx

These examples are not reported because they use valid label reference syntax: `[guide][]`, `[guide]`, and `[this][guide]`.

```markdown
Read the [guide][], the [guide], or [this][guide].

[guide]: https://example.com/guide
```

--------------------------------

### Disallowed hook usage in test setup

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/vitest/no-hooks.mdx

An example of test setup using `beforeEach` that triggers a lint rule report.

```ts
import { beforeEach, expect, test } from "vitest";

let cart;

beforeEach(() => {
  cart = createCart();
});

test("starts empty", () => {
  expect(cart.items).toEqual([]);
});
```

--------------------------------

### Set up toolchains and run homepage benchmarks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/bench/site/README.md

Sets up required toolchains and repositories, then executes the benchmark suite using a specified Bun binary under test. Supports running full suites, specific sub-benchmarks, or quick smoke tests via environment variables.

```sh
bench/site/setup-toolchains.sh                      # node, deno, pnpm/yarn/npm, bun release + canary -> $SITEBENCH_HOME/toolchains
bench/site/setup-repos.sh                           # rolldown/benchmarks clone + deps of bench/express, bench/websocket-server, bench/postgres
BUN=/abs/path/to/bun bench/site/run-all.sh          # everything: bundler http ws postgres install (~30 min with RUNS=3)
BUN=/abs/path/to/bun bench/site/run-all.sh http ws  # a subset
RUNS=1 BUN=... bench/site/run-all.sh                # quick smoke run
```

### Correct test title starting with lowercase letter

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/jest/prefer-lowercase-title.mdx

An example of a test title starting with a lowercase letter, which complies with the rule.

```ts
import { expect, test } from "@jest/globals";

test("adds an item", () => {
  expect(cart.add(item)).toBe(1);
});
```

An example of a test title starting with an uppercase letter, which is reported by the rule.

```ts
import { expect, test } from "@jest/globals";

test("Adds an item", () => {
  expect(cart.add(item)).toBe(1);
});

--------------------------------

### Install GCC 11 on Ubuntu with apt

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/project/contributing.mdx

Installs gcc-11 and g++-11. If the package cannot be located, add the ubuntu-toolchain-r/test PPA and run apt install again.

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install gcc-11 g++-11
# If the above command fails with `Unable to locate package gcc-11` we need
# to add the APT repository
sudo add-apt-repository -y ppa:ubuntu-toolchain-r/test
# Now run `apt install` again
sudo apt install gcc-11 g++-11
```

### Initialize project and install Drizzle and Neon dependencies

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/neon-drizzle.mdx

```sh
mkdir bun-drizzle-neon
cd bun-drizzle-neon
bun init -y
bun add drizzle-orm @neondatabase/serverless
bun add -D drizzle-kit
```

### Install in production mode with bun install --production

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx

Installs without devDependencies. --production implies --frozen-lockfile and only controls what gets installed; devDependencies already in node_modules remain. Use bun prune --production to remove them.

```bash
bun install --production
```

--------------------------------

### Valid test setup inside hooks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/bun-test/require-hook.mdx

Example of compliant test structure with setup logic placed inside `beforeAll` and `beforeEach` hooks.

```ts
import { beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, mock, setDefaultTimeout, test } from "bun:test";

setDefaultTimeout(10_000);
mock.module("./mailer", () => ({ send: mock() }));

const names = ["ada", "grace"];
let db;

beforeAll(() => {
  db = connect();
  db.seed(names);
});

describe("users", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    clearCache();
  });

  test("finds a user", () => {
    expect(db.find("ada")).toBeDefined();
  });
});
```

### False positive example when combining flags

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/oxc/bad-bitwise-operator.mdx

Example pattern where bitwise flag combining gets reported because the right-hand operand is a property access.

```js
const mode = flags | Mode.Write;

```

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/vitest/no-hooks.mdx

An example of self-contained test setup that avoids shared hook state and passes the lint rule.

```ts
import { expect, test } from "vitest";

test("starts empty", () => {
  const cart = createCart();
  expect(cart.items).toEqual([]);
});
```

### Valid comments example

Demonstrates allowed comments: starting with an uppercase letter, starting with a number, containing a URL, or matching tool directives like eslint-disable.

```js
// Retry once, then give up
await send(message);

// 3 attempts at most
// https://example.com/retries explains why
/* eslint-disable-next-line no-console */
console.log("sent");
```

### Add start script to package.json

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/quickstart.mdx

Configure a start script in package.json to run the TypeScript entrypoint with Bun.

```json
{
  "name": "my-app",
  "module": "index.ts",
  "type": "module",
  "private": true,
  "scripts": { // [!code ++]
    "start": "bun run index.ts" // [!code ++]
  }, // [!code ++]
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/bun": "latest"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "typescript": "^7"
  }
}
```

### Get nanoseconds since process start with Bun.nanoseconds()

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/utils.mdx

Returns the number of nanoseconds since the current bun process started, as a number. Useful for high-precision timing and benchmarking.

```ts
Bun.nanoseconds();
// => 7288958
```

--------------------------------

### Global test setup with beforeAll and afterAll hooks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/test/configuration.mdx

Define database setup and teardown handlers using `bun:test` hooks in a preload script.

```typescript
// Global test setup
import { beforeAll, afterAll } from "bun:test";

beforeAll(() => {
  // Set up test database
  setupTestDatabase();
});

afterAll(() => {
  // Clean up
  cleanupTestDatabase();
});
```

### Valid interface with grouped overloads

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/typescript/adjacent-overload-signatures.mdx

Example not reported by the rule because all overload signatures for get are grouped consecutively.

interface Storage {
  get(key: string): string;
  get(key: string, fallback: string): string;
  clear(): void;
}
```

### Preconnect at startup using --fetch-preconnect flag

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/networking/fetch.mdx

Pass `--fetch-preconnect` to the Bun CLI to initiate preconnecting to a host upon startup. Note that this flag is not implemented on Windows.

```sh
bun --fetch-preconnect https://bun.com ./my-script.ts
```

--------------------------------

### bunx command syntax

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/snippets/cli/bunx.mdx

General invocation form for bunx. Executes an npm package executable (CLI); if the package isn't installed in node_modules, Bun installs it into a global shared cache.

```bash
bunx [flags] <package>[@version] [flags and arguments for the package]
```

--------------------------------

### Install Build Tools with Scoop on x64

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/project/building-windows.mdx

Installs Scoop and the remaining tools (nodejs-lts, go, rustup, nasm, ruby, perl, ccache). LLVM is installed separately because Scoop is buggy when installing llvm alongside the rest.

```powershell
irm https://get.scoop.sh | iex
scoop install nodejs-lts go rustup nasm ruby perl ccache
# scoop seems to be buggy if you install llvm and the rest at the same time
scoop install llvm@23.1.1
```

### Start the SvelteKit development server with Bun

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/sveltekit.mdx

Run the development server using Bun with the `--bun` flag. Omit `--bun` if you want to run the dev server with Node.js instead.

```sh
cd my-app
bun --bun run dev
```

```txt
  $ vite dev
  Forced re-optimization of dependencies

    VITE v5.4.10  ready in 424 ms

    ➜  Local:   http://localhost:5173/
    ➜  Network: use --host to expose
    ➜  press h + enter to show help
```

--------------------------------

### Install with symlink backend and run with --preserve-symlinks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx

With --backend=symlink, Node.js won't resolve node_modules of dependencies unless each dependency has its own node_modules folder or you pass --preserve-symlinks to node or bun. The example installs with the symlink backend, then runs a file under bun and node with --preserve-symlinks.

```bash
rm -rf node_modules
bun install --backend symlink
bun --preserve-symlinks ./my-file.js
node --preserve-symlinks ./my-file.js # https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#--preserve-symlinks
```

### Incorrect label reference with whitespace

### Reported usage of beforeEach hook

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/jest/no-hooks.mdx

Example of test setup using `beforeEach` that triggers the `jest/no-hooks` lint rule violation.

```ts
import { beforeEach, expect, test } from "@jest/globals";

let cart;

beforeEach(() => {
  cart = createCart();
});

test("starts empty", () => {
  expect(cart.items).toEqual([]);
});
```

--------------------------------

### Get prototype with Object.getPrototypeOf

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/perf/everyday/objects.txt

Compares the prototype of class instances against a class prototype.

```typescript
class Base {}
class Derived extends Base {}
const instances = [new Base(), new Derived()];
function turn(i: number): number {
  return Object.getPrototypeOf(instances[i & 1]!) === Derived.prototype ? 1 : 0;
}
```

### Serve frontend with Bun.serve and HTML imports

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/src/runtime/cli/init/rule.md

Demonstrates setting up a full-stack server using Bun.serve with route handlers, WebSockets, HTML imports, and React/CSS bundling. Run index.ts using bun --hot for hot reloading.

```ts
import index from "./index.html"

Bun.serve({
  routes: {
    "/": index,
    "/api/users/:id": {
      GET: (req) => {
        return new Response(JSON.stringify({ id: req.params.id }));
      },
    },
  },
  // optional websocket support
  websocket: {
    open: (ws) => {
      ws.send("Hello, world!");
    },
    message: (ws, message) => {
      ws.send(message);
    },
    close: (ws) => {
      // handle close
    }
  },
  development: {
    hmr: true,
    console: true,
  }
})
```

```html
<html>
  <body>
    <h1>Hello, world!</h1>
    <script type="module" src="./frontend.tsx"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

```tsx
import React from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";

// import .css files directly and it works
import './index.css';

const root = createRoot(document.body);

export default function Frontend() {
  return <h1>Hello, world!</h1>;
}

root.render(<Frontend />);
```

```sh
bun --hot ./index.ts
```

### Avoid reporting by not exporting unimported functions

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/import/no-unused-modules.mdx

Example setup where `formatTime` in `shop/format.js` is not exported, avoiding lint warnings for unused exports.

```json
{
  "root": true,
  "plugins": ["import"],
  "parserOptions": { "ecmaVersion": "latest", "sourceType": "module" },
  "rules": { "import/no-unused-modules": ["error", { "unusedExports": true }] }
}
```

```js
import { formatDate } from "./format.js";

console.log(formatDate(new Date()));
```

```js
export function formatDate(date) {}
function formatTime(date) {}
```

### Restricted modifier example (reported)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/bun-test/no-restricted-matchers.mdx

Demonstrates that restricting a modifier such as `{ resolves = "" }` causes all chains starting with `resolves` to be reported.

```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

test("loads the user", async () => {
  await expect(loadUser(1)).resolves.toEqual({ id: 1 });
  await expect(loadUser(2)).resolves.not.toBeNull();
});
```

### builder.onStart(callback)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/bundler/esbuild.mdx

Registers a callback that is called when the bundle starts. This hook is useful for initialization tasks before the bundling process begins.

```APIDOC
## builder.onStart(callback)

### Description
Registers a callback that is called when the bundle starts. This hook is useful for initialization tasks before the bundling process begins.

### Method
builder.onStart(callback: () => void): void

### Parameters
- **callback** (function) - Required - A function to be called when the bundle starts.

### Example
```ts
builder.onStart(() => {
  console.log('Bundle started');
});
```
```

### Implement a custom Bun plugin

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/bundler/fullstack.mdx

Create a plugin that exports a BunPlugin object with a name and setup function. The example loads .custom files as JavaScript modules.

```typescript
import type { BunPlugin } from "bun";

const myPlugin: BunPlugin = {
  name: "my-custom-plugin",
  setup(build) {
    // Plugin implementation
    build.onLoad({ filter: /\.custom$/ }, async args => {
      const text = await Bun.file(args.path).text();
      return {
        contents: `export default ${JSON.stringify(text)};`,
        loader: "js",
      };
    });
  },
};

export default myPlugin;
```

--------------------------------

### Generic Box class

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/perf/everyday/kinds-of-types.txt

`Box<T>` stores a value of type `T` and `get(): T` returns it; instantiated here as `Box<number>`.

```typescript
class Box<T> { constructor(public value: T) {} get(): T { return this.value; } }
const boxes: Box<number>[] = [new Box(1), new Box(2), new Box(3), new Box(4)];
function turn(i: number): number {
  return boxes[i & 3].get() + 1;
}
```

### Autolink URLs with paths

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/js/bun/md/spec-permissive-autolinks.txt

Matches optional URL paths starting with '/' and delimited by slashes. Non-alphanumerical characters (., -, _) in path components must be bounded by alphanumerical characters.

```example
https://example.com/images/branding/logo_272x92.png
.
<p><a href="https://example.com/images/branding/logo_272x92.png">https://example.com/images/branding/logo_272x92.png</a></p>
.
--fpermissive-url-autolinks
```

describe("cart", () => {

  test.skip("adds an item", () => {

});

### Look up a numeric enum name by value

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/perf/everyday/classes.txt

Uses reverse mapping Status[i % 3] to get the enum member name and returns its length.

```typescript
enum Status {
  Active,
  Paused,
  Stopped,
}
function turn(i: number): number {
  return Status[i % 3]!.length;
}
```

### Install and run Bun in a GitHub Actions workflow

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/runtime/cicd.mdx

Use the oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 action to install Bun in a GitHub Actions runner and execute bun or bunx commands.

```yaml
name: my-workflow
jobs:
  my-job:
    name: my-job
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # ...
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 # [!code ++]

      # run any `bun` or `bunx` command
      - run: bun install # [!code ++]
      - run: bun index.ts # [!code ++]
      - run: bun run build # [!code ++]
```

### ArrayBufferSink.prototype.start(options?)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/streams.mdx

Configures and starts the sink with buffer allocation and streaming options.

```APIDOC
## start(options?)

### Description
Initializes the internal buffer and streaming settings for the sink.

### Syntax
```ts
sink.start(options?: {
  asUint8Array?: boolean;
  highWaterMark?: number;
  stream?: boolean;
}): void;
```

### Parameters
- **options** (object) - Optional configuration object.
  - **asUint8Array** (boolean) - Optional. If set, output is returned as a `Uint8Array`.
  - **highWaterMark** (number) - Optional. Preallocates an internal buffer of this size to improve performance with small chunk sizes.
  - **stream** (boolean) - Optional. On `flush()`, returns written data as `Uint8Array` / `ArrayBuffer` and restarts writes from the beginning of the buffer.

### Return Value
- `void`
```

--------------------------------

### Set scanner credentials via environment variables

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/security-scanner-api.mdx

Some enterprise scanners read authentication from environment variables. Export the required variables (for example in ~/.bashrc) before running bun install so the scanner uses them automatically.

```bash
# This might go in ~/.bashrc, for example
export SECURITY_API_KEY="your-api-key"

# The scanner will now use these credentials automatically
bun install
```

### Invalid test code violating require-hook

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/bun-test/require-hook.mdx

Example of invalid test setup where initialized `let` variables and standalone function calls are placed outside hooks at the top level or directly in a `describe` block.

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";

let db = connect();
db.seed(["ada", "grace"]);

describe("users", () => {
  clearCache();

  test("finds a user", () => {
    expect(db.find("ada")).toBeDefined();
  });
});
```

### Define an HTTP route and start an Elysia server in server.ts

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/elysia.mdx

Define a GET route at root using Elysia and listen on port 8080. Logs the running server port using the app.server instance.

```ts
import { Elysia } from "elysia";

const app = new Elysia().get("/", () => "Hello Elysia").listen(8080);

console.log(`🦊 Elysia is running on port ${app.server?.port}...`);
```

### Report child process resource usage with resourceUsage()

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/child-process.mdx

After the spawned process exits, call resourceUsage() to get maxRSS and CPU time. The example spawns bun --version and logs memory and CPU usage.

```typescript
const proc = Bun.spawn(["bun", "--version"]);
await proc.exited;

const usage = proc.resourceUsage();
console.log(`Max memory used: ${usage.maxRSS} bytes`);
console.log(`CPU time (user): ${usage.cpuTime.user} µs`);
console.log(`CPU time (system): ${usage.cpuTime.system} µs`);
```

--------------------------------

### onStart

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/bundler/plugins.mdx

Registers a callback that runs when the bundler starts a new bundle. The callback may return a Promise, and the bundler waits until all onStart callbacks have completed before continuing.

```APIDOC
## onStart

### Description
Registers a callback that runs when the bundler starts a new bundle. The callback can return a Promise; after the bundle process has initialized, the bundler waits until all `onStart()` callbacks have completed before continuing.

### Signature
```ts
onStart(callback: () => void | Promise<void>): void;
```

### Parameters
- **callback** (function) - Required - A function that runs when the bundler starts a new bundle. May return `void` or `Promise<void>`.

### Notes
- `onStart()` callbacks (like every other lifecycle callback) cannot modify the `build.config` object. To mutate `build.config`, do so directly in the `setup()` function.

### Example
```ts
await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ["./app.ts"],
  plugins: [
    {
      name: "onStart example",
      setup(build) {
        build.onStart(() => {
          console.log("Bundle started!");
        });
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

### Example (async callbacks)
```ts
const result = await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ["./app.ts"],
  outdir: "./dist",
  sourcemap: "external",
  plugins: [
    {
      name: "Sleep for 10 seconds",
      setup(build) {
        build.onStart(async () => {
          await Bun.sleep(10_000);
        });
      },
    },
    {
      name: "Log bundle time to a file",
      setup(build) {
        build.onStart(async () => {
          const now = Date.now();
          await Bun.$`echo ${now} > bundle-time.txt`;
        });
      },
    },
  ],
});
```
```

### Create and run a new Elysia project using bun create

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/elysia.mdx

Initialize a new Elysia application in Bun, enter the project directory, and start the development server with hot reloading.

```bash
bun create elysia myapp
cd myapp
bun run dev
```

### Install LLVM 23 via package managers

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/project/contributing.mdx

Bun requires LLVM 23.1.1; a mismatched version causes memory allocation failures at runtime. Choose the command for your platform.

```bash
brew install llvm@23
```

```bash
# LLVM has an automatic installation script that is compatible with all versions of Ubuntu
wget https://apt.llvm.org/llvm.sh -O - | sudo bash -s -- 23 all
```

```bash
sudo pacman -S llvm clang lld
```

```bash
sudo dnf install llvm clang lld-devel
```

```bash
sudo zypper install clang23 lld23 llvm23
```

### Install dependencies and run benchmark suites

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/bench/README.md

Run benchmarks directly from the bench directory after installing required benchmark dependencies such as mitata. Specify a custom runtime binary by setting environment variables like BUN or modifying the .env file.

```bash
# run from this directory. bench/ has its own package.json and bun.lock,
# the repo root does not install benchmark dependencies such as mitata.
bun install

bun run ffi
bun run log
bun run gzip
bun run async
bun run sqlite

# to use custom version of bun/deno/node binary
BUN=path/to/bun bun run ffi
# or edit .env file
```

### package.json with a metadependency

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/overrides.mdx

Example package.json where foo depends on bar, making bar a metadependency. By default, Bun installs the latest version of all dependencies and metadependencies according to the ranges specified in each package's package.json.

```json
{
  "name": "my-app",
  "dependencies": {
    "foo": "^2.0.0"
  }
}
```

### Configure Bun.Image constructor options

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/image.mdx

Pass configuration options to protect against decompression bombs with `maxPixels` and control automatic EXIF orientation with `autoOrient`.

```ts
new Bun.Image(input, {
  // Reject if width*height > this. Checked after reading the header,
  // before allocating the pixel buffer. Default matches Sharp (~268 MP).
  maxPixels: 4096 * 4096,
  // Apply JPEG EXIF Orientation before any other op. Default: true.
  autoOrient: true,
});
```

--------------------------------

### Configure install.ca and install.cafile

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/bunfig.mdx

To configure a CA certificate, set install.ca to the certificate string or install.cafile to the path of a certificate file. Set one of the two. If both are set, only cafile is used. --ca or --cafile on the command line replaces both.

```toml
[install]
# The CA certificate as a string
ca = "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"

# A path to a CA certificate file. The file can contain multiple certificates.
cafile = "path/to/cafile"
```

--------------------------------

### Retrieve rows as raw Buffers with sql.raw()

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/sql.mdx

Use .raw() to get rows as arrays of Buffer objects (Uint8Array on SQLite). Call .raw() before the query starts (before await, .then(), or .execute()) to ensure binary formats are requested.

```ts
const rows = await sql`SELECT * FROM users`.raw();
console.log(rows); // [[Buffer, Buffer], [Buffer, Buffer], [Buffer, Buffer]]
```

--------------------------------

### Serve static files with Bun.serve

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/http/stream-file.mdx

Implement a basic static file server by combining Bun.file with Bun.serve.

```typescript
// static file server
Bun.serve({
  async fetch(req) {
    const path = new URL(req.url).pathname;
    const file = Bun.file(path);
    return new Response(file);
  },
});
```

--------------------------------

### Read a resolved promise's value with Bun.peek()

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/utils.mdx

Use Bun.peek() to read a promise's result without await or .then, but only if the promise has already fulfilled or rejected. This example shows peeking a resolved promise to get its value.

```typescript
import { peek } from "bun";

const promise = Promise.resolve("hi");

// no await!
const result = peek(promise);
console.log(result); // "hi"
```
